propositions: The comment-hygiene gate is wired into CI as a standalone step but is not exposed via `make lint`, causing local lint to pass while CI rejects the same tree, surfacing failures only after review
Running `scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py` as part of `make lint` costs ~4.9s and moves baseline from 17.8s to ~22.7s, acceptable given the 15-minute CI cycle cost of misses
No deliberate intent to exclude the gate from `make lint` exists in the introducing ticket; the pattern mirrors the env-registry drift-gate precedent already documented in the Makefile
The `lint` target must invoke `python scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py` alongside `scripts/gen_env_registry.py --check` to align local and CI verdicts
A wiring test using the `_lint_target_body` idiom must verify the gate is invoked in the lint target, with teeth proving the assertion fails when the invocation is removed
